Columns include tce_period, tce_time0bt, tce_depth, tce_duration, tce_model_snr, tce_prad, tce_ntoi, tce_steff, tce_sradius.

TESScut already serves Sectors 108 and 109 (the sector in progress) because MAST ingests FFIs roughly weekly; LC/TP/DV for S108 are not out. The fresh-sector window via cutouts is therefore ~1-5 weeks ahead of the 24-39 d LC release and 4-11 months ahead of TOIs.

TESS-SPOC does include faint nearby M dwarfs through its 'within 100 pc' rule: per-sector target lists at https://archive.stsci.edu/hlsps/tess-spoc/target_lists/s00NN.csv (header line '#TIC_ID,RA,DEC'; parse with skiprows=1) contain 1,936 (S85), 3,704 (S69), 3,838 (S31) of the 100,567 faint-M pool, including 520-1,103 stars with T>15 per sector. QLP target lists (https://archive.stsci.edu/hlsps/qlp/target_lists/s00NN.csv; 1,066,502 rows in S85, 1,152,719 in S104) contain ~3,000-3,300 pool members per sector but none fainter than T=15. A random 60-star census found 51/60 with at least one public product (TESS-SPOC 38, TARS 50, QLP 32, eleanor-lite 26, TGLC 22, T16 20, TASOC 11, SPOC 2-min 7) and 9/60 with nothing - so ~15% of the pool needs home-made photometry for ALL sectors and most of the rest need it for SOME sectors.

The TESS Input Catalog is still v8.2, built on Gaia DR2 with Bailer-Jones (2018) distances and a curated Cool Dwarf list; there is no Gaia DR3 update (Hardegree-Ullman et al. 2026, arXiv:2603.28850). A full TIC/Gaia DR3 cross-match is downloadable at https://exofop.ipac.caltech.edu/tess/gaiadr3_tic_crossmatch.php (also in the NASA Exoplanet Archive; notebook at https://github.com/kevinkhu/ticgaia). Any d<100 pc / Teff<3900 K selection made from TIC 'd' and 'Teff' should be re-derived with Gaia DR3 parallaxes and colours before claiming distances or radii.

tglc 0.8.1 (PyPI, 2026-09-19) requires Python >=3.10,<3.13; the project venv is Python 3.13, so TGLC must be run from a separate 3.12 environment (and separately from MIT QLP, which also installs as 'tglc').

Gaia DR3 vari_planetary_transit was replaced on 2023-02-07 after an erroneous first release (old table renamed vari_planetary_transit_13june2022); only the replacement should be used for cross-matching. Gaia DR4 timeline: archive offline 25 Nov 2026 12:00 CET, DR4 live 2 Dec 2026 12:00 CET (ESA notice 8 Oct 2026). DR3 sample gives mean 35.3 matched FoV transits per source over 34 months, so DR4 will average ~68 over 66 months.

The spoc-s14-s86 multi-sector TOI stream is not a faint-star stream (25 TOIs since July 2026 span T 8.6-15.0, median 11.6) and the top CTOI submitter overall is lafargamagro (1,173 CTOIs), not montalto (1,076); faint CTOIs (T>13.5) come from montalto 96, bouma 43, nardiello 35, olmschenk 30, wilson 27, jroth 17, feliz 16.

K2 superstamps are not entirely unsearched: Nardiello et al. 2016 (arXiv:1608.08539, M67 in K2 C5) report 'three planetary candidates'; Libralato et al. 2016 (arXiv:1510.09180, M35/NGC 2158 in C0) reach Kp~24 at 10% in 6.5 h; Soares-Furtado et al. 2017 (arXiv:1703.00030) did image subtraction on the C0 superstamp. PSFK2 exists at https://archive.stsci.edu/hlsp/psfk2 even though the K2 HLSP index page omits it.

Kepler Bonus light-curve files are named by KIC (hlsp_kbonus-bkg_kepler_kepler_kic-005689121_kepler_v1.0_lc.fits) with HDU LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED and columns FLUX (PSF), SAP_FLUX, PSF_FLAT_FLUX, FLATTEN_MASK, SAP_QUALITY; 27,495 of the 29,800 M-star catalogue rows have a KIC number, so 'background' in KBONUS mostly means 'KIC star that was never a Kepler target', not 'uncatalogued star'. For Kuber's 'exclude primary targets' step (1,836 -> 1,800) use the set of all tpforg values in the source catalogue (every KIC that has a TPF) or MAST Kepler target search; the TAP table q1_q17_dr25_stellar is 'not available for querying' (keplerstellar, 990,244 per-quarter rows, is).

HEASARC lists Sector 99 twice (2026 Jan 05-15 and Jan 22-Feb 02) around the 3I/ATLAS sector 1751 (Jan 15-22); the QLP timing bug starts at Orbit 210 = 'second half of Sector 99'. Any lag computation or ephemeris work on S99 must pick the end date explicitly.

Caldwell et al. 2020 (TESS-SPOC) is arXiv:2011.05495; Eisner et al. 2021 PHT II is arXiv:2011.13944 (90 candidates, 73 single-transit, 85%/51% recovery for >4 Re / 3-4 Re); Salinas et al. 2025 is arXiv:2502.07542 (214 candidates with Rp>0.27 RJ, 88 single-transit, 122 multi, 4 multi-planet, S1-26); Ment & Charbonneau 2023 is arXiv:2302.04242, AJ 165, 265 (363 M dwarfs 0.1-0.3 Msun within 15 pc, S1-42, P<7 d, 2-min, modified BLS); DTARPS II (Melton et al. 2024, AJ 167, 203; arXiv:2302.06724) searched 976,814 Year-1 southern stars -> 462 candidates + 310 spatially-incomplete Galactic-plane objects, 58% new; Kunimoto 2021 QLP EM paper is arXiv:2110.05542 (9.1M stars S27-39, ~1M/sector, T<13.5); Huang 2020 QLP is arXiv:2011.06459 (RNAAS 4, 204 and 206).

TESScut operational limits for a bulk FFI-photometry job: cutout area <= 10,000 pixels, <= 5 requests/s per user (503 otherwise), SPOC FFIs only for S91+ (TICA cutouts discontinued August 2025); plan for ~5-10 cutouts/s across the whole job, not per worker.

FFI cadence history matters for duration grids and injection tests: 30 min in the Prime Mission (S1-26), 10 min in EM1 (S27-55), 200 s from EM2 (S56 onward); EM3 runs September 2025-September 2028 with ~13,000 2-min and ~2,500 20-s targets per sector (Guide to TESS for EM planning).
